books.section: B. The Fall of the Berlin Wall and the End of the Cold War
The Presidency of George H. W. Bush

stem: Which of the following best explains why the Berlin Wall fell in 1989 rather than in an earlier decade?

options.text: The United States had withdrawn all of its troops from West Berlin
options.misconception: American troops remained in West Berlin until after reunification; no withdrawal caused the fall.

options.text: The Soviet Union had signed a treaty promising to tear the Wall down
options.misconception: No such treaty existed; the Wall fell because of protests and Soviet non-intervention, not a treaty.

options.text: Gorbachev's reforms and his refusal to use Soviet force let protests succeed
East Germany had voted to join NATO in a national referendum
options.misconception: No such referendum happened; East Germany joined the West through reunification in 1990.

rationales.A: American troops stayed in West Berlin through 1989. Background: the Wall fell because of events in the East, not an American withdrawal.
rationales.B: The photograph shows no treaty about the Wall. Background: Moscow never agreed to tear the Wall down; East Germany opened it under pressure from protests.
rationales.C: Background: Gorbachev loosened Soviet control of Eastern Europe and made clear he would not send tanks to save Communist governments, as earlier Soviet leaders had. With that threat gone, mass protests in Poland and East Germany toppled the regimes, and the Wall came down.
rationales.D: East Germany never held a referendum on joining NATO. Background: reunification in 1990 brought the eastern states into the Federal Republic, which was already in NATO.
rationales.general:
1. Ask what was different about 1989. The Wall had stood for twenty-eight years, through many protests.
2. Background: earlier Soviet leaders had sent tanks to crush reform movements, in Hungary in 1956 and Czechoslovakia in 1968.
3. Background: Gorbachev broke that pattern. His reforms loosened control, and he refused to use force to save the Communist regimes.
4. Once the threat of Soviet tanks was gone, protests that would once have been crushed were able to topple the governments.
Remember: the Wall fell when Moscow stopped holding it up.

stimulus.text: Photograph of a man on a ladder using a hammer and chisel to chip a piece from the Berlin Wall at Potsdamer Platz, Berlin, November 1989. The Wall's western face is covered in colorful graffiti, and a crowd watches from below.
